title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page computes the p-adic valuation of the divided powers of p, p^{(n)} = p^n/n!, in Z_p. This is the basic estimate needed to see whether the divided-power ideal pZ_p is topologically PD-nilpotent. That question governs convergence in a divided-power de Rham / crystalline complex, and it is where p = 2 differs from odd p.

(1) Legendre's formula: v_p(n!) = (n - s_p(n))/(p-1), where s_p(n) is the base-p digit sum (Grothendieck writes 'chiffr_p n').

(2) Hence v_p(p^n/n!) = ((p-2)n + s_p(n))/(p-1). For p = 2 this equals s_2(n).

(3) Define gamma_{p,i} = inf_{n>=i} v_p(p^{(n)}). He notes that n -> v_p(p^{(n)}) is neither increasing nor decreasing, so the inf is needed.
- For p = 2, gamma_{2,i} = 1, attained at powers of 2. So the divided powers of 2 never become more divisible.
- For p odd, gamma_{p,i} >= ((p-2)i+1)/(p-1), which tends to infinity. So pZ_p is topologically PD-nilpotent exactly when p is odd.

(4) He then compares consecutive terms. Write i = (p-1) + (p-1)p + ... + (p-1)p^{s-1} + i_s p^s + ... + i_r p^r with i_s < p-1, so s is the number of trailing digits equal to p-1. Then s_p(i) = (p-1)s + sum_{alpha>=s} i_alpha and s_p(i+1) = 1 + sum_{alpha>=s} i_alpha. He derives a criterion for v_p(p^{(i)}) <= v_p(p^{(i+1)}).

(5) Application: gamma_{p,i} = min(v_p(p^{(i)}), gamma_{p,i+1}). So gamma_{p,i} = gamma_{p,i+1} as soon as v_p(p^{(i+1)}) <= v_p(p^{(i)}). He concludes this holds when i+1 ≡ 0 mod p, i.e. when i = p*l - 1.
errors: In the comparison of consecutive terms the carry '+1' is dropped. The correct inequality reads (p-2)i + (p-1)s + Σ_{α≥s} i_α ≤ (p-2)(i+1) + 1 + Σ_{α≥s} i_α. The exact difference is v_p(p^{(i+1)}) - v_p(p^{(i)}) = 1 - s, not ((p-2) - (p-1)s)/(p-1).

Consequently the stated equivalence [v(i) ≤ v(i+1)] ⇔ [(p-1)s ≤ p-2] ⇔ [s=0] is wrong. The correct criterion is s ≤ 1, i.e. i+1 not divisible by p^2. Strict inequality v(i) < v(i+1) holds iff s = 0, i.e. i+1 not divisible by p.
Despite this slip, the final sufficient condition for gamma_{p,i} = gamma_{p,i+1} remains correct. Indeed v(i+1) ≤ v(i) iff s ≥ 1 iff i+1 ≡ 0 (mod p), i.e. i = p*l - 1.
Minor: the lower bound for p ≠ 2 is written '> (p-2)/(p-1) n' with n where i is meant. Strictly, ≥ ((p-2)i+1)/(p-1).

ideas.what: Legendre's formula for v_p(n!) via base-p digit sum
Valuation of the divided powers p^n/n! and the inf over n ≥ i; p=2 versus p odd dichotomy
ideas.modern_name: Topological PD-nilpotence of (p) in Z_p (divided powers on pZ_p are PD-nilpotent iff p odd)
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's published texts to my knowledge. Background to his crystalline programme (Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, 1968).

ideas.what: Monotonicity of n -> v_p(p^n/n!) controlled by trailing (p-1)-digits of n

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine scratch computation of p-adic valuations of divided powers, a standard ingredient of crystalline theory. It is notable only as a working trace (including a small arithmetic slip) behind the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex.
transcription_corrections: '[-inf_p-]' is a struck-out false start ('Si p' or similar), not 'inf_p'.
The marginal note reads 'cette fonction en n n'est ni croissante ni décroissante...'; the transcription is essentially right.
The line '(avec p^{s+1}-1 [?])' is an underbrace label: the first block of digits sums to p^s - 1 (the handwriting shows p^{s+1}-1 corrected). This is not a separate condition.
In the line i+1 = ..., the leading term is (i_s+1)p^s (the carry), which the transcription and apparently Grothendieck render as i_s p^s.
The final lines read 'il suffit que l'on ait v_p(p^{(i+1)}) ≤ v_p(p^{(i)}), i.e. que i+1 ≡ 0 (p), i.e. i de la forme pl - 1'.
